2026-11-09 targeted, key x509 fits (was unverified under dotnet). RFC 5280 6.1: a path must satisfy "(a) for all x in {1, ..., n-1}, the subject of certificate x is the issuer of certificate x+1; (b) certificate 1 is issued by the trust anchor". 6.1.3(a)(1), for each certificate i: "The signature on the certificate can be verified using ... the working_public_key"; 6.1.4(d): "Assign the certificate subjectPublicKey to working_public_key" (per step). Outcome already run: SameSubjectFromAnotherRoot_IsNotTrusted passes.

2026-11-09 targeted, key x509 fits. RFC 5280 Sec. 8 (Security Considerations): "compromise of a CA's private signing key may have a catastrophic effect. If an attacker obtains the private key unnoticed, the attacker may issue bogus certificates"; "CAs are advised to implement a combination of strong technical measures (e.g., tamper-resistant cryptographic modules)". The 6.1 path conditions test names, signatures and validity only, not who asked for the name.
